lede: Joseph D'Arcy is the first person in this archive's English line — baptised at Portsea on 19 March 1780, son of Robert and Jean, the record that survived inside a twenty-two-month transcript. After that he disappeared. He signed his sister's marriage at Chatham in 1806 and then nothing, for a hundred and forty years of family memory. Here is the rest of him.

death.notice: London Evening Standard, Friday 11 February 1848, page 4
death.text: On the 7th inst., at Homestead, Lymington, Hants, LIEUTENANT COLONEL D'ARCY, LATE ROYAL ARTILLERY, K.L.S., in the 69th year of his age.
death.reg: Death registered at Lymington, Hampshire, March quarter 1848 — volume 8, page 159

will.text: LIEUTENANT-COLONEL JOSEPH D'ARCY, [late] of the Royal Artillery, formerly of PRIESTLANDS, NEAR LYMINGTON, but late of HOME MEAD, SOUTHAMPTON, who died on the 7th of February, at the age of 69, had EXECUTED HIS WILL IN THE MONTH OF FEBRUARY, 1844, leaving …
will.cut: The article goes on to summarise what he left, and the digitised text stops there. The will itself was proved in 1848 and is at Kew.

kls.head: And three letters after his name
kls.body: One notice gives him as “Lieutenant Colonel D'Arcy, late Royal Artillery, K.L.S.” — Knight of the Royal Order of the Lion and Sun, a Persian decoration. It was given to British officers who served on the missions to the Shah's army in the 1810s and 1820s.
kls.careful: This archive has not yet traced his Persian service, and will not assert it from three letters. What the letters establish is that he held a foreign order, which for a Royal Artillery officer of that generation points one way.

career: Baptised at Portsea St Mary, son of ROBERT and JEAN
“Commenced his military career at the taking of St Domingo”
In the Royal Artillery officers' list
Witness at his sister Margarett Maria Isabella's marriage at Chatham
At the taking of Walcheren; and served in Sicily
FIVE YEARS IN PERSIA in the service of Prince Abbas Mirza — and Knight of the Lion and Sun
Executes his will, leaving his property to his wife Katherine
Dies at Home Mead, Lymington, in his 68th year
son: And he left at least one son. The Cork Daily Herald of 3 October 1863 carries a marriage at Lymington of a D'Arcy “son of the late Colonel D'Arcy, R.A.” — the same town, fifteen years on. The OCR loses the groom's forename.
age: Two wrinkles, both stated rather than smoothed. The papers cannot agree whether he died in his 68th or 69th year — 68th fits the Portsea baptism of March 1780 almost exactly. And if he began at St Domingo in 1793 he was thirteen, which is early even for that army. A boy of thirteen could go as a cadet or a volunteer and be commissioned at fifteen, which is what the Royal Artillery list showing him from 1795 would then mean. It is also possible the obituarist rounded a date fifty-five years old.
matters: The archive now holds Robert D'Arcy's marriage, his career, his death and his funeral; his son George Pitt D'Arcy's marriage and Irish service; and his son Joseph's whole life — Saint-Domingue, Sicily, Walcheren, five years in Persia with the Shah's son, a Persian knighthood, a house in Hampshire and a widow named Katherine. Three years ago the family tree had a name and a rumour of Yorkshire.

obit.papers: Morning Herald (London), 29 February 1848, p.4 · Saunders's News-Letter (Dublin), 2 March 1848 · Lincolnshire Chronicle, 3 March 1848, p.6
obit.text: Died, on the 7th of February, at his residence, HOME MEAD, LYMINGTON, HAMPSHIRE, in his 68th year, LIEUT. COLONEL D'ARCY, LATE OF THE ROYAL ARTILLERY. He commenced his military career at THE TAKING OF ST. DOMINGO IN 1793; he served also IN SICILY and at THE TAKING OF WALCHEREN; he was FIVE YEARS IN PERSIA IN THE SERVICE OF PRINCE ABBAS MIRZA, son [of the] King of Persia, who for …
obit.note: Three papers carried the same notice and the digitised text breaks in a different place in each; the wording above is assembled from all three, with the breaks marked.

persia.head: Five years in Persia
persia.body: ABBAS MIRZA was the Qajar crown prince, and in the 1810s and 1820s he was rebuilding the Persian army on a European model with British officers to help him. That is what Joseph D'Arcy was doing there, and it is why a separate notice gives him as K.L.S. — Knight of the Royal Order of the Lion and the Sun, the Shah's decoration.
persia.careful: The archive now has the service from an obituary and the order from a death notice, which corroborate each other. It has not yet seen a service record, and does not know the years.

katherine.head: And a wife named Katherine
katherine.body: The Lady's Newspaper of 8 April 1848 carried the same will summary as the Morning Post and got a little further before the scan fails: he left his “property to his wife, KATHE[RINE] D'ARCY, to which she h[as] …”
katherine.means: A name this archive did not have. Joseph D'Arcy married, and his widow outlived him.

census.ref: 1841 census · PRIESTLANDS, Milford, Lymington, Hampshire · HO107/393 book 4, folio 3, page 1, schedule 352
census.note: Twenty people under one roof: the family, a brother, a Mrs Pitt, and eleven servants.
rows: his wife — the “Kathe[rine]” of the will
of Joseph's own generation, in Joseph's house
and this is the surname that has been sitting in this family's names for two centuries
census.servants: Then eleven more: Laura Dillard, Joseph Hyde, Charles Hamby, Thomas Williams, Mary Finch, Jane Jennings, Ann Russ, Harriet Marshall, Rachael Barter, Loise Croucher and Jane Viney. A household of twenty with eleven servants is a gentleman's establishment, not a half-pay officer's cottage.

hampshire.head: Born in Hampshire
hampshire.body: The 1841 census gives Joseph's birth county as HAMPSHIRE and his age as 61, which is a birth in 1780. Portsea is in Hampshire. This is independent corroboration of the baptism of 19 March 1780 — the entry that survives only because it falls inside a twenty-two-month transcript — from a census taken sixty-one years later.

pitt.head: Elizabeth Pitt, aged 55
pitt.body: Living in the house in 1841, between the youngest child and the servants, is an ELIZABETH PITT, born about 1786. This archive's line runs through GEORGE PITT D'ARCY — the name recurs for four generations, down to a George Pitt D'Arcy born at Brisbane in 1864 — and nobody has ever known where the Pitt came from.
pitt.careful: A census does not say who she was. She is not called a relative, because the 1841 census does not record relationships at all. What can be said is that a woman named Pitt was living in the household of Robert D'Arcy's son in 1841, and that Robert D'Arcy's other son had carried Pitt as a middle name since 1783. That is a connection worth chasing and it is not yet an explanation.
pitt.chip: a lead, and a good one
pitt.tested: Tested and still open. Elizabeth Pitt's death was registered at Lymington in 1851, so she stayed in the district after Joseph died — but no newspaper death notice for her survives to say what she was to the family, and the 1841 census records no relationships. The Pitt question is exactly where it was, with one more fact around it.

richard: And a RICHARD DARCY, aged 57, born about 1784 — in the house, of Joseph's own generation and a year younger than George Pitt D'Arcy. The archive has never heard of him. Robert and Jean married at Portsea in June 1779 and baptised Joseph there in March 1780; a Richard of 1784 fits that family exactly, and the Portsea transcript stops in 1782 so his baptism would never have been found in it. Searched for him across Hampshire in every record type and found nothing further: he is a name, an age and an address, in his brother's house.

after.head: After him
rows: PRIESTLANDS is broken into lots and advertised for sale — “Lot 5, Higher Priestlands; Lot 6, Lower Priestlands” — Exeter Flying Post, 19 October 1848
ELIZABETH PITT dies at Lymington, her death registered in the district. She had not moved away
“Mrs. D'Arcy … 5 0” subscribes to a Lymington public fund got up by the Mayor, among the local clergy and gentry — Hampshire Advertiser. The widow was still in the town four years on
after.note: She is not in the 1851 census under any Darcy spelling in Hampshire, which is a gap in the index rather than a departure — the subscription list puts her there the following February.

forward.head: The branch that stayed in England
forward.body: The archive has said for a year that Joseph's line simply stopped. It did not. His son FRANK, aged two at Priestlands on census night in 1841, is FRANK HYDE D'ARCY, and he married ANNA MARIA SIMPSON at Lymington on 29 September 1863 — daughter of R. Salisbury Simpson, her residence given as Bengal. The marriage was announced in Thacker's Overland News for India and the Colonies on 3 October 1863.
rows: D'ARCY BIRTH NOTICES at Lymington in the British and Irish newspaper indexes — five of them
ELIZABETH ELEANOR D'ARCY born at Lymington
FRANK HYDE D'ARCY marries ANNA MARIA SIMPSON at Lymington
KATHERINE LUCY ELIZABETH D'ARCY dies at Lymington
EMILY L. B. D'ARCY born at Lymington
forward.means: Fifty-two D'Arcy records at Lymington, running from Joseph's death in 1848 through to an electoral roll of 2021. This is a living English branch of the same family, and it has never been part of this archive. The tree is not the authority here — these people are not on it — so they belong on the new generations page and not in the pedigree.

duty.head: And the will has a second document
duty.body: JOSEPH D'ARCY of Lymington, Hampshire, grant year 1848, court “PCC and Country Courts” — Index to Death Duty Registers 1796-1903, The National Archives IR 27/284. The Death Duty register behind that index (IR 26) states the value of the estate and names the legatees and executors, often in more detail than the will itself. That is now two documents at Kew rather than one, and the index reference for finding them.
